info.name: Airline Ticketing System - Interview and E2E

description.content:
# Airline Ticketing System - interview and E2E

Start the backend with `docker compose up --build -d --wait`. Select **ATS Local** (baseUrl http://localhost:8080, no trailing slash), or edit the collection's baseUrl fallback. The backend has no authentication; do not add your Postman management API key to backend requests.

**Short demo:** Run folder **01 Interview demo**. Fresh schedule/date/reference variables are generated automatically. Follow create -> search -> visual seat map -> atomic group booking -> conflict/rollback -> cancel -> rebook -> cleanup. Seat-map responses have a **Visualize** tab.

**Full verification:** Run the entire collection from the first request in order, one iteration. All folders depend on the initialized run and earlier fixtures. Includes all three seeded aircraft, validation/protocol failures and no-write proofs, inclusive/exclusive booking-window boundaries, sold-out/full-group cancellation, concurrent booking/cancellation, and a real UTC departure cutoff. The last folder waits about 15-75 seconds using bounded polling; use Runner, not individual Send, for this folder.

Fresh eight-character flight IDs prevent rerun collisions. The successful run cancels every future reservation it creates. Immutable schedules, cancelled history and one intentionally retained departed confirmed reservation remain. Stop-on-failure is recommended: interrupted/failed runs can leave future reservations and must be inspected using saved references, not blindly retried.

FR1/2 seed details are observed indirectly through valid airport/aircraft usage and complete layouts; there are intentionally no airport/aircraft CRUD endpoints. Healthy public HTTP checks do not prove database-fault rollback, outages/503 recovery, SQL plans, internal logging/MDC privacy, deterministic barriers, multi-JVM behavior or production load capacity. Those are covered separately by Maven integration tests. This collection does not add fault-injection APIs or claim to exercise unexpected 500/503 responses.

Only postman.json and env.json belong in this directory. Newman installation and reports are external to the repository.
